items.title: Weather-normalised energy baselines
items.why: One regression equation per meter (energy against cooling degree days and occupancy). Standard IPMVP Option C / ASHRAE Guideline 14 method; no ML training.
items.other_inputs: Weather API (hourly outdoor temperature); building calendar.
logic: Daily total per meter; exclude offline or bad-quality values.
Cooling degree days from outdoor temperature (base temperature configurable, e.g. 18 °C).
Fit daily kWh = a + b × CDD + c × occupancy on the last 3–12 months.
Accept only if CV(RMSE) and NMBE meet ASHRAE Guideline 14.
Daily: expected vs actual; refit monthly.
items.output: AI tags per meter, daily: expected kWh, deviation kWh and %.
items.example: Main meter, 21 Nov: actual 18,420 kWh; expected 16,950 kWh (CDD 14.2, 1,850 people); +8.7%, flagged above ±5%.
items.history: 3 months to start; 12 for all seasons

items.title: Energy conservation recommendations
items.why: Fixed rules on live points (running outside schedule, unoccupied zones, excess fresh air); savings from measured kW. The agent writes each recommendation.
items.other_inputs: Operating hours; rated fan kW per AHU/FCU (no fan power point); tariff.
logic: R1 out of hours: unit running while its schedule is off, 30 min or more.
R2 unoccupied: zone or lighting occupancy false for 60 min while the unit or lights run.
R3 fresh air: outdoor-air damper above 50% while CO2 is below 600 ppm.
Saving = hours × kW × tariff; rank by monthly cost. Thresholds are examples.
items.output: Ranked recommendation list with evidence points and estimated monthly saving.
items.example: AHU-03 ran 41 h outside schedule last week (run ON, schedule OFF, fan 85%). Fix the weekend schedule; about 1,150 kWh per month.
missing: Fan power (kW) per AHU and FCU: not in the list; use rated kW from the asset register

items.title: Chilled-water setpoint reset recommendations
items.why: Trim-and-respond rules (ASHRAE Guideline 36 approach) with fixed limits; the operator approves each change. No forecasting.
items.other_inputs: Which AHUs and FCUs the plant serves; setpoint limits agreed with the owner and chiller OEM.
logic: Every 15 min: no valve above 90% and zones satisfied for 2 h → recommend +0.5 °C.
2 or more valves above 95% or a zone warm by 1.5 °C → recommend −0.5 °C.
Limits 6.0–9.0 °C; max one change per hour; skip if zone humidity would exceed 60%.
items.output: Setpoint recommendation in the operator queue: current, recommended, reason, limits, status.
items.example: CH-01: chilled_water_supply_temperature_setpoint 6.5 → 7.0 °C. Highest valve 62% for 2 h; all zones within ±1 °C. Awaiting approval.

items.title: Sub-meter balance and drift alerts
items.why: Parent minus the sum of sub-meters is arithmetic; drift is a CUSUM of the gap to the baseline.
logic: Daily unaccounted = main − sum of sub-meters; flag above 5% for 3 days.
CUSUM of deviation from baseline; flag past 10% of a normal week.
Skip days with meter offline.
items.output: Meter alerts; AI tags unaccounted % and drift flag.
items.example: Main meter vs 6 sub-meters: 11.8% unaccounted for 5 days; sub-meter SM-4 flat since 16 Nov.
items.history: Balance from day 1; drift after 3 months

items.title: Energy cost of each fault
items.why: Extra kWh during the fault × tariff.
items.other_inputs: Fault start and end from the FDD engine; tariff; asset-to-meter mapping.
logic: Extra kWh = (actual kW − expected kW) × duration.
No power point: rated kW × duration, marked as an estimate.
Cost = extra kWh × tariff.
items.output: Extra kWh, cost and basis on each fault alert.
items.example: CH-01 low delta-T, 6.5 h: extra 310 kWh (measured).

items.title: Alarm fatigue reduction
items.why: ISA-18.2 and EEMUA 191 alarm statistics (rates, chattering, standing alarms, bad actors) plus co-occurrence; the agent writes shift summaries.
items.other_inputs: Alarm and event journal from the platform.
logic: Rate per operator per hour; floods; chattering (3+ in 1 min); standing (24 h+).
Top 10 bad actors; alarms that start together on linked equipment.
Recommend delay, re-limit or grouping for engineers to apply.
items.output: Weekly alarm KPI report, recommended changes, shift summaries.
items.example: Week 47: 20 alarms per hour (ISA-18.2 guidance about 6). FCU-12 zone deviation chattering 610 times; add a 5-min delay.

items.title: Work-order prioritisation by SLA
items.why: Weighted score plus median resolution times from history.
items.other_inputs: Asset criticality register; SLA target per priority.
logic: Score = criticality × priority × SLA proximity.
Typical fix time per work type and team = median of 6 months.
At risk when time left < typical fix time.
items.output: Ranked queue and daily supervisor summary.
items.example: WO-1042 chiller trip: 3 h to SLA, typical fix 4.5 h, at risk; Team A suggested.
missing: Asset criticality register (master data, not a point)

items.title: Natural-language questions on building data
items.why: The language model reads the question and writes the answer; read-only tools return every number.
items.other_inputs: All points through read-only tools; the list shows typical ones.
logic: Router picks a specialist agent.
Agent calls parameterised read-only tools.
Model answers from tool results only, with the data basis.
items.output: Answers with a table or chart and the points used.
items.example: Asked which floors had high CO2 with low occupancy: L8-East 1,240 ppm at 14:00 with 22 people; outdoor-air damper at 10%.

items.title: Carbon trajectory to 2030
items.why: Energy × emission factor, projected with and without planned measures.
items.other_inputs: 2030 target; planned measures; grid emission factor (configured).
logic: Monthly tCO2e = kWh × emission factor.
Project business as usual and with planned measures to 2030.
Gap to target per year.
items.output: Trajectory table and chart with summary.
items.example: 2026: 4,120 tCO2e; 2030 business as usual 3,980; with measures 3,310; target 3,000.
missing: Carbon intensity factor: not in the list; configure it in the platform
